title: ReadingScheme
description: A reading scheme (ADR 0109): how a token's pinned reading is written, such as Jyutping, Pinyin, Baxter's Middle Chinese, sitelen Lasina, the Tiberian reading or Attic with its vowel lengths. Data in profiles/schemes/<id>.yaml: the pipeline reads it (nabu.schemes, which adds what voices do with readings) and core gets it through @nabu/schema/schemes. What a scheme can be used for follows from what it gives: shown as options or asked for (`answer`), typed (`typed`), heard as tones (`tones`).
$comment: v0. A profile's reading layer (`annotations`, kind reading) and a course voice's `reading` and `pronounce` name a scheme by its id.

name.description: What the UI calls it: Jyutping, Middle Chinese (Baxter).

language.description: The language whose sounds it writes: yue for Jyutping, cmn for Pinyin, ltc for Baxter's Middle Chinese. The audio round trip compares a language's characters by their readings where a scheme of that language can read written text (nabu.schemes).

lang.description: The language tag of its text where it stands on its own, as an option or an answer: yue-Latn-HK-jyutping. A profile's reading layer may tag its ruby otherwise (`lang`, ADR 0071).

answer.description: The orthography its readings are in where a card offers them as options or asks for one (char-read, reading-disambiguation, transcribe; ADR 0098). A scheme without one is shown, never asked: Pinyin and Baxter in Classical Chinese.

typed.description: A learner may type a reading in it (transcribe, ADR 0054). A typed answer is lowercased in `locale`, what may stand `between` syllables is dropped, and what is left must be syllables of this shape, end to end.

syllable.description: One syllable, as a regular expression that JavaScript and Python's `regex` read alike (letters, character classes, quantifiers): [a-z]+[1-6].

between.description: A character class of what may stand between syllables and is dropped: spaces, apostrophes, dots, hyphens.

tones.description: Its syllables carry tones (Jyutping's numbers): what marks one, and each tone's pitch, which the tone exercises, the device's tone scoring and the IPA voices take use.

system.description: The tone system's id, as tone exercises name it: yue-jyutping.

marks.description: A character class of what marks a tone in a syllable: [0-9]. A syllable's tone is its marks; a typed answer with none has no tones.

values.description: Each tone, keyed by its marks, in the order a learner meets them.

name.description: What the UI calls its pitch: high level, low rising.

letters.description: Its contour in Chao's tone letters, 1 lowest to 5 highest: 55, 35, 21. Voices that take IPA get them as ˥˧˩.

checked.description: Its shorter contour in a checked syllable (one ending in a stop), where it has one: 5.

shape.description: Its pitch's movement, which the device judges when it cannot tell the speaker's register.

template.description: Chao letters at the start, middle and end of a syllable that the device's tone classifier compares a heard contour with. REVIEW: from the standard descriptions; tune on native recordings.
